thread.title: GE’s 111-year run in the Dow comes to an end - MarketWatch

author: Jeremy C. Owens
title: GE’s 111-year run in the Dow comes to an end - MarketWatch
text:
General Electric Co. is losing an important title it has held for more than a century: Dow Jones Industrial Average component.
GE GE, -1.89% , which was part of the Dow Jones index DJIA, -1.15% when it was started in 1896 and had been a part of the blue-chip portfolio continuously since 1907, is being replaced by Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. WBA, +0.72% , S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Tuesday afternoon.
“The U.S. economy has changed: Consumer, finance, health care and technology companies are more prominent today and the relative importance of industrial companies is less,” David Blitzer, managing director and chairman of the index committee at S&P Dow Jones Indices, explained in Tuesday’s announcement. “Today’s change to the DJIA will make the index a better measure of the economy and the stock market.”
Opinion: Why adding Twitter to the S&P 500 could be a ‘sell’ signal for the stock
GE has been removed from the index twice previously, but has been a constant presence since replacing Tennessee Coal & Iron in 1907. The other companies that were part of the index when GE entered in 1907: Amalgamated Copper, American Car & Foundry, American Smelting & Refining, American Sugar, Colorado Fuel & Iron, National Lead, Peoples Gas, U.S. Rubber, U.S. Rubber 1st preferred, U.S. Steel and U.S. Steel preferred.
GE has fallen on hard times in recent years though, with a plunging stock price that broke an unwritten rule for the Dow : A component’s stock should not be worth less than 10% of the highest-priced stock in the index. GE closed at $12.95 a share Tuesday, which was less than 1/20 the price of a share of Boeing Co. BA, -3.84% .
Previously: GE shocks market with multibillion-dollar loss in legacy reinsurance business
S&P Dow Jones Indices noted that GE’s plunging stock price factored into the decision as well.
“The DJIA is a price-weighted index, and the range of prices among its 30 constitutes matter. The low price of GE shares means the company has a weight in the index of less than one-half of 1 percentage point,” the announcement noted. “Walgreens Boots Alliance’s share price is higher, and it will contribute more meaningfully to the index.”
The change might not be a bad thing for GE investors, though. Companies that were dismissed from the index in the past five years have generally performed better than their replacements after the changes . This will be the first change in the Dow since Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.62% replaced AT&T Inc. T, +0.62% in 2015.
The change is set to take effect before the market opens next Tuesday, June 26. GE stock fell more than 1.5% in late trading after the announcement was made, while Walgreens shares rose more than 2.5%.
MarketWatch staff writer Tomi Kilgore contributed to this article.
